answers.name: the guided reading list
answers.unclear: Only whether a five-row, hand-picked set should be called a registry with list added, or just a list. The poster says to add every word that applies, so I kept both. One entry per document, kept current, chosen by hand (registries.csv marks it curated).

answers.name: the tracker registry
answers.unclear: Each entry shows task counts by status but has no status of its own. I left 'tracker' off because the poster's test is 'each entry carries a status', and a tracker instance carries only its tasks' statuses.

answers.name: the outpost observation stream
answers.unclear: Each row is a dated reading of one file's state on the work computer (installed, verified, differs), and 'a reading, kept as of its date' is how the poster describes a snapshot. I chose stream because rows are appended as observations happen and never rewritten. The poster gives no way to separate a stream of readings from a snapshot. The file is currently header-only, so I judged it from its README and its check.

answers.collection: window.__traffic, the traffic ledger in web-tools lib/gh-boot.js
answers.name: the open tab's capped call record
answers.unclear: Each entry is a request event. It is pushed when the call goes out, then rewritten (status, ms, wire, error, and msg via __noteApiError) until the call settles, which is the empty box's 'record rewritten until its event ends'. But the poster lists 'the traffic logs' as a stream example, and the code calls this a ledger. Those logs turn out to be the separate files in web-tools-private logs/traffic/ written by lib/kits/traffic-log.js. The array also drops its oldest rows past CAP=400, which is open call 4 ('window'), and none of the four add-on words covers that.

answers.name: the sessions cache
answers.unclear: Each row is a session, an event whose record is re-summarized whenever its blob sha moves, so it is rewritten while the session is live: the poster's own example for the empty box. It is folded from sessions/ records, so it is a cache. Each row carries a closing state (merged, done, pending, needs...), which I read as a tracker status, though that state is a session's self-report rather than a work item's open or done. Rows are capped at 400 newest, which is open call 4 again.

answers.name: source snapshots (dated intakes)
answers.unclear: A bundle is either one dated intake that is never revised (a snapshot) or a series that gains intakes over time and whose 'acquired' moves to the latest. A series is a thing that changes, holding snapshots inside it, closer to registry or stream. In budget-drs, fn-data-drs is even a re-imported mirror, which is a cache. The poster has no rule for a collection whose entries fall in two boxes, or for a series of snapshots. I chose by the dominant case, the dated intake folders.

answers.name: the enacted budget decision history (a cache)
answers.unclear: Each row is a line movement in a budget session, an enacted decision that does not change, so I chose stream. But it is not 'added to as things happen': it is rebuilt wholesale from one dated pull (2026-06-04 longitudinal) plus authored driver rules, and a rule change rewrites rows. That could also read as a snapshot (a reading of 2019-2026 as of the pull). Base-phase rows are levels, not events. The poster does not say whether a cache is boxed by what its rows describe or by the rebuild that rewrites them.

answers.name: the errand request queue
answers.unclear: This is exactly open call 3: request files never change and are closed by adding a result file, and the poster says they are not snapshots and offers 'request queue' only as a recommendation. 'Tracker' applies only loosely, because an errand's status (open, claimed, closed) comes from which files exist beside the request rather than a field the entry carries. A ping's result file is also rewritten until 'settled', which is empty-box behavior inside the same collection.

poster: The two-question grid settled the clean cases quickly: a curated set of documents (registry plus list), a generated roster of trackers (registry plus cache), and an append-only observation file (stream). The add-on words, and the fix showing that the atlas is a cache rather than a snapshot, kept me from mistaking derived files for readings. It failed in four places. First, the second question ('does it change after it is written') has no clear answer for a cache, since every rebuild rewrites its rows, and that left the decision ledger and the sessions cache undecided. Second, 'thing versus event' is undefined for readings and observations, so observations.csv and the decision ledger could each sit in two boxes. Third, its own examples point the wrong way for the traffic ledger: 'the traffic logs' sits under stream, yet window.__traffic rows are rewritten until each call settles, which by the rule is the empty box. Fourth, it has no rule for a collection whose entries are of two kinds (source bundles: dated intakes versus series). Caps (call 4) and request files (call 3) are left open while they decide items 4, 5 and 8.
